The Story

Chapter One — The Lodger

In the winter of 1974 your grandfather rented the attic room of Hollowmere House to a quiet man who paid a year in advance and never gave a name. In the spring the house burned. Everyone got out. The lodger did not.

Forty years later your brother Elias bought the ruin, wrote you eleven letters about restoring it, then wrote a twelfth: "The wiring is fine. It's the house that keeps switching itself on."

Tonight you let yourself in. The power is dead, the fuse box is stripped, and something on the ground floor is walking with a limp it did not have an hour ago.

What walks the ground floor is not the lodger any more. Something came up out of the cellar wearing what was left of him: a bald slab of a man, stripped to the waist, his jaw strapped into a studded leather muzzle with the teeth pushing out through it, and a long forged blade run out of each wrist. The fire took his eyes and left two coals in the sockets. He finds you the only way left to him — he listens.

Controls

W A S D — move  ·  Mouse — look  ·  Shift — run
Ctrl — crouch (quiet)  ·  F — torch  ·  E — interact / read
Esc — pause  ·  E at a wardrobe or bed — hide inside it
1 — bare hands  ·  2 — pistol  ·  3 — shotgun  ·  4 — claw hammer  ·  Q — swap
H — first aid tin (fixes a leg a trap has ruined)
Left click — fire  ·  Right click / Space — torch flash in his face
G — set a bear trap on the boards where you stand
A pistol round puts him down for 15 seconds. Buckshot puts him down for 30. A trap costs him 9 and a boot.
Nothing in this house can kill him, and every shot tells him exactly where you are standing.

Six things stand between you and the street:
1. Four fuses, and a screwdriver to get the fuse box cover off.
2. Three numbers on three scraps of paper, for the strongbox keypad.
3. The front door key, inside the strongbox.
4. Three boards nailed across the door — crowbar.
5. A chain and a padlock — bolt cutters.
6. A lock seized solid with rust — oil can.
Two interior doors are padlocked as well. The lockpicks open those.
Every one of those jobs makes noise, and he is listening to all of it.
He is blind. He hears running, and he hears you — the game listens to your microphone.
Crouch, move slowly, and keep your room silent. Watch the Noise meter. Nothing is recorded.

End of Chapter One

The cold outside is real cold, the kind that has weather in it. Behind you every window of Hollowmere House is lit, warm and yellow, the way a home looks when someone is waiting up.

You never found Elias. You found his coat, his notes, and a man in the hallway with your brother's wristwatch on.
